solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nation's lubricant, allegedly

indicators.note: allegedly hints that the word is only claimed, i.e. said to be, so we go by how it is pronounced

parts.note: grease is a thick lubricant for machinery

explanation.surface: A country is said to be the slippery stuff of the world, perhaps a jibe at its economy.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a European country, so it is an example of a nation.

clue.text: Hollow Holy Grail's recast in flashy fashion

indicators.note: recast means cast again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
a hollow word is emptied of its inside, leaving only the outer letters of Holy

parts.note: the word Grail with the S of its 's included

explanation.surface: Someone has remade the sacred cup in a gaudy style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow' reduces Holy to HY; with GRAILS that makes HYGRAILS, which 'recast' rearranges. Here the 's of Grail's counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means gaudy and showy, so doing something garishly is doing it in a flashy manner.

clue.text: Estate manager finding old, old coin on hill

parts.note: ex- as in ex-wife means former or old
the ecu was an old French coin
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An estate manager discovers an ancient coin lying on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: An executor manages and distributes the estate of a person who has died.

clue.text: Without hesitation, girl has cold vegetable

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the girl's name goes round the hesitation

parts.note: Celia is a girl's name
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A girl without a moment's pause has a chilled vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' reads as 'promptly', but 'Without' here is the old word for outside, so the girl's name goes round the hesitation sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeriac is a root vegetable, a variety of celery grown for its knobbly bulb.

clue.text: Second bit of musician's equipment left out of range

indicators.note: out of says the letter for left is taken away from the word for the guitarist's pick

parts.note: a plectrum is the small pick a guitarist strums with

explanation.surface: A second piece of a musician's kit has been left out of the band's range.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range, as in the whole spectrum of opinion.

clue.text: Rapid revision concealing name of poet from 1 across

indicators.note: concealing says the rearranged letters hide the abbreviation for name within them
a revision reworks something, so the letters of Rapid are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hasty edit hides the name of a poet from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' turns RAPID into PIDAR, and 'concealing' puts N inside it. '1 across' points to the answer of that clue, the country, so the definition is a Greek poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pindar was an ancient Greek lyric poet, famous for his odes to victorious athletes.

clue.text: Well-padded nymphomaniac's last diminutive partner

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word nymphomaniac's

parts.note: hubby is the pet form of husband, a partner

explanation.surface: A nymphomaniac's most recent little man turns out to be well-padded.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby means plump, so a chubby person is well-padded.

clue.text: York, joining navy, given new lease of life

indicators.note: joining here means getting inside, so the city's old name enters the navy's letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
Ebor is the Latin-derived short name for York, as in the Archbishop of York's signature

explanation.surface: A York man who joins the navy finds a new life.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebor is used for York (Archbishops of York sign Ebor). Joining the navy, it sits between R and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Reborn means brought back to life, revived or renewed in spirit.

clue.text: Once again beat up and kill?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: re- as a prefix means again
to drum is to beat

explanation.surface: Do you beat someone up a second time, and then kill them?
explanation.walkthrough: REDRUM read upwards in the grid; famously REDRUM is the reversed word scrawled in The Shining.
explanation.definitionFit: To murder is to kill unlawfully and deliberately.

clue.text: Law restricting the Spanish reception room

indicators.note: restricting says the word for law hems in, i.e. contains, the Spanish article

parts.note: a rule is a law
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A regulation keeps the Spanish out of the reception room.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruelle was the bedroom in which French ladies of fashion held morning receptions.

clue.text: Burden with indicator of additive including carbon

indicators.note: including says the code holds the chemical symbol within it

parts.note: an E number is the label code given to a food additive
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A food label burdened with an additive code that contains carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: To encumber is to burden or weigh down.

clue.text: Short emission from wimp bearing right

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the word for wimp carries the letter for right inside it

parts.note: a squit is a small, insignificant person, a wimp

explanation.surface: A brief spurt comes from a weakling who is heading right.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUIT is British slang for a puny person.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirt is a quick jet of liquid, a short emission from a nozzle.

clue.text: Apostle almost welcoming dullard to beano

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the shortened name goes round the dullard
almost says the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: James was one of the twelve apostles
a bore is a dull person

explanation.surface: An apostle nearly opens his arms to a tedious type at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the apostle by his last letter. A beano is British slang for a lively party or knees-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large festive gathering, just like a beano or celebration.

clue.text: Composer finding one high-scoring card between two others

indicators.note: between says the middle pieces are placed inside the two card letters

parts.note: J and K are other cards, the jack and king
an means one
the ace is the card that often scores highest

explanation.surface: A composer finds he holds one top card sandwiched by two more.
explanation.definitionFit: Leos Janacek was a Czech composer of operas such as Jenufa.

clue.text: 4s not beginning to weave rug

indicators.note: to weave is to interlace threads, so the remaining letters are woven into a new order
not beginning says the plural loses its first letter

parts.note: the answer to 4 across in the plural, spectra

explanation.surface: Ranges of colour, though not starting, are woven into a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is SPECTRUM, so '4s' is SPECTRA; 'not beginning' drops the S to leave PECTRA, and 'to weave' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet is a woven floor covering, a large rug.

clue.text: Scrubber returning dessert with sigh of relief

indicators.note: returning says the pudding word is read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding
ah is what someone says on a sigh of relief

explanation.surface: Someone sends back their pudding with a contented sigh.
explanation.walkthrough: A FOOL is a British pudding of fruit puree folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried gourd fibre sponge used for scrubbing in the bath.

clue.text: Lousy actor permitted role ill-suited to him?

parts.note: a ham is a bad, over-acting performer
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A poor actor has been allowed a part he can't carry off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads back from the wordplay: the great tragic part is not one for a ham.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is Shakespeare's most demanding title part, hardly one for a bad performer.

clue.text: See 15
Beast of burden eating artist's sweet

indicators.note: eating says the animal swallows, i.e. contains, the artist's letters

parts.note: a camel carries loads, a beast of burden
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A pack animal eats a painter's sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a chewy sweet made from boiled sugar and butter.

clue.text: Sex in single file voluntarily given up

indicators.note: given up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone has willingly given up their sex life, perhaps to queue in single file.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'given up' reads upward: the run singlE FILE VOLuntarily backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sex as in one's sex life, the romantic and sexual side of a person's life.

clue.text: Waste of n2?

indicators.note: to waste here is to wreck or ruin, so the spoken form of the expression is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: n with a superscript 2 is read aloud as n squared

explanation.surface: A maths teacher frets over a pointless squared term.
explanation.walkthrough: Read n2 as 'n squared'; 'Waste' rearranges SQUARED N. The whole clue is also the definition: wrecking 'n squared' is itself squandering.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander is to waste, and here the very act of scrambling the expression is the waste.

clue.text: Grammatical unit feeling heartless

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: sentience is the capacity for feeling

explanation.surface: A cold, unfeeling grammar rule.
explanation.walkthrough: SENTIENCE has nine letters; 'heartless' drops the fifth, I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is the basic grammatical unit containing a subject and verb.

clue.text: Resort forever wanting energy to get measure of twist

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word for forever is dropped from the resort

parts.note: Torquay is a seaside resort in Devon
ay or aye is an old word for ever, forever
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A resort that perpetually lacks energy gets measured for twisting.
explanation.walkthrough: TORQUAY is an English seaside resort in Devon; AY (ever, as in 'for aye') goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Torque is the turning force, the measure of twisting effect in physics.

clue.text: Final remark from Charterhouse's first hopeless case

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Charterhouse's

parts.note: a loser is a hopeless case

explanation.surface: The last word on the school's first hopeless pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: Charterhouse is an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: A closer is a closing remark, the final thing said.

clue.text: Involve broken toenail (nothing missing)

indicators.note: broken signals the letters are rearranged
missing says the round letter for nothing is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A broken toenail but nothing missing, the doctor reassures.
explanation.walkthrough: '(nothing missing)' drops O from TOENAIL, leaving TENAIL, which 'broken' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or require something as a consequence.

clue.text: Some kine go missing, having been raised by woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the run is read upwards, backwards
some says only some of the letters in the phrase are wanted, a run within it

explanation.surface: Some cattle have gone missing, after being reared by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: kiNE GO MIssing; 'having been raised' reads it upward. Kine is an old plural of cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is a woman's name, the heroine of Shakespeare's Cymbeline.

clue.text: See 13
Upper down under swallowed by rising fish

indicators.note: swallowed by says the slang for Australia goes inside the fish
in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
Oz is slang for Australia, down under

explanation.surface: A drug from Australia gulped down by a fish swimming upward.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the fish upward. 'Upper' is slang for a stimulant or mood-lifting drug, not the adjective it poses as.
explanation.definitionFit: Prozac is an antidepressant, a mood-lifting drug loosely called an upper.

clue.text: Prominent feature of frolic involving an old currency

indicators.note: involving means wrapping in, so the frolic surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun, a frolic
DM is the Deutschmark, the former German currency

explanation.surface: A notable highlight of the jaunt involves some old money.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a prominent feature of a landscape, easily seen and recognised.

clue.text: Go back in captivity, losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart says the middle letter is removed
back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: trapped means held in captivity

explanation.surface: Someone returns to prison and loses all courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TRAPPED into DEPPART; 'losing heart' drops its central P.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away or leave.

clue.text: Gutter-dwellers backing the likes of Oscar Wilde, reportedly, to engage in astronomy

indicators.note: backing says the gutter animals' word is read backwards

parts.note: rats live in gutters and drains

indicators.note: reportedly says we go by how the word is said, not spelt

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was gay, so people like him are gays

explanation.surface: We are all in the gutter, but some are looking at the stars, as Wilde himself put it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on Wilde's line about lying in the gutter while looking at the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: To stargaze is to watch the stars, a basic form of astronomy.

clue.text: Increase scope to cover Sweden's porting record

indicators.note: to cover says the word for broaden goes over and round the Swedish letter

parts.note: to widen is to increase scope

indicators.note: the port side is the left, so this takes the leftmost letter of Sweden's

explanation.surface: Sweden widens its scope to carry a shipping record.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the left side of a ship, so 'porting' points to the leftmost letter. Wisden is the annual almanack of cricket records.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisden is the cricket almanack, a book of record of the game's statistics.

clue.text: Turn over and kiss on top, maybe

parts.note: to roll is to turn over
to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: Roll over and kiss on top of the bed, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-neck is a jumper with a high folded collar, an example of a top.

clue.text: Fraction of a minute qualification

definitions.meaning: a ... of arc is one three-hundred-and-sixtieth part of a full circle, a fraction of it
a university award such as a BA or BSc

explanation.walkthrough: 'of a minute' plays on angle units: a minute of arc is a sixtieth of the first sense, which is itself a fraction of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic award such as a BA is a qualification; a unit of angle is a fraction of a circle.
